title: the-commit-fans-out-to-its-subscribers
intention: A git commit is an event any component can answer: one system-owned post-commit hook runs every component's own post-commit subscriber, so codemother gets each commit on its bus verb `commit` without the heartbeat polling git.
why: Akien 2026-09-30: "NOTHING in the system that should fire on the heartbeat execpt the messaging"; "all probes respond to events". 164da559823d deletes every groundloop/pulse.py, and cairn/devices/codemother/groundloop/pulse.py is the only thing that hands codemother a commit (it polls git HEAD each beat and calls watch.on_commit). Deleting it without an event in its place leaves the watcher dark; git allows one installed post-commit, and counting_block (5a4ec289bf15) already holds it, so a second component can only answer the commit through a fan-out.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule enforced by physics: the commit itself fires the subscribers) and RULE 1 (each component answers the commit through its own hook and codemother is reached only through its bus verb); the 2026-09-30 ruling 'nothing fires on the heartbeat but the messaging' and a-probe-needs-a-consumer ('name the EVENT that fires it')
how: The installed .git/hooks/post-commit becomes a fan-out owned by a tool (no state of its own): it lists tracked files named hooks/post-commit under components (git ls-files, no master index — each component declares its own), runs each with the repo root, never blocks the commit, and prints a refusal by name. counting_block's existing hooks/post-commit becomes one subscriber instead of the installed hook (its install-hook/verify-hook move to the fan-out's door). codemother gains hooks/post-commit that posts {hash, files, message} to its own `commit` bus verb through bus_client (the bus is a store, so a commit made while codemother is down waits in its mailbox instead of being missed). The same build deletes cairn/devices/codemother/groundloop/pulse.py, the beat's HEAD poller, with its TestPulse teeth: left standing beside the subscriber it would hand on_commit every commit twice. 164da559823d depends_on this and deletes the other eight pulses.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) a commit in the main tree does not run every tracked */hooks/post-commit subscriber (counting_block's fold and codemother's post both fire, each once); (2) codemother's bus mailbox does not receive a `commit` envelope carrying the new hash and its changed files; (3) a failing subscriber blocks or aborts the commit or silences the others; (4) anything still reads git HEAD on the beat to find commits. WRONG INTENT if a component needs the commit before it lands (that is pre-commit, the tester's) or if the fan-out had to hold state of its own. Horizon: the first ten commits after the build.
watchme: none, because the falsifier is read on every commit by records that already exist: codemother's activation files under ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/watch/activations/ (written by cairn/devices/codemother/watch.py on_commit) and the counting block's fold printed by cairn/machines/counting_block/__main__.py pulse; a commit with neither is the red, with nothing further to learn after ten commits.
children: none, because the whole change is one tool plus two subscriber files; 164da559823d is a dependant, not a child.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where does the tool live? cairn/tools/post_commit/ with intention+why.json, fanout.py (discover + run), hooks/post-commit (the installed body, marker cairn-post-commit-fanout), and __main__ with install-hook / verify-hook copied in shape from cairn/machines/counting_block/hook.py. (2) How are subscribers found? `git ls-files -z '*/hooks/post-commit'` from the repo root, excluding cairn/tools/post_commit/hooks/post-commit itself; each run as an executable with cwd=repo root, its exit code and stderr recorded in the run's printed summary, a non-zero exit never aborts the others and the hook always exits 0. (3) What does codemother's subscriber post? cairn/devices/codemother/hooks/post-commit runs a codemother-owned module that reads HEAD, `git diff-tree --no-commit-id -r --name-only HEAD`, the subject line, and posts verb `commit` to codemother through cairn.tools.bus_client (its published client tool). (4) What happens to counting_block? its hooks/post-commit body stays as the subscriber; hook.py install/verify are removed and its verify-hook CLI delegates to the fan-out's verify (the counting_block proof's verify-hook tooth must stay green). (5) What proves it? one proof under cairn/tools/post_commit/proofs/ committing in a throwaway repo with two stub subscribers (one failing) and asserting both ran and the commit landed; plus a live tooth that the installed hook is ours and identical to the tracked body.

decisions.text: D1 (measured 2026-10-02): of the nine tracked */groundloop/pulse.py, only cairn/devices/codemother/groundloop/pulse.py reads git HEAD (grep HEAD|rev-parse|git log over every one). Adding codemother's post-commit subscriber while that pulse stands would hand watch.on_commit each commit twice, once from the hook and once from the beat, and falsifier (4) would stay red. So this build deletes it and the TestPulse class in cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_watch.py that patches it, and the docstring of cairn/devices/codemother/probes/commit_fires_activations.py stops naming it. codemother stays on the roster through its probes/ folder. 164da559823d keeps the other eight pulses.

D2 THE FAN-OUT (cairn/tools/post_commit/fanout.py, new; empty cairn/tools/post_commit/__init__.py beside it). Constants: REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]; HOOK_SOURCE = Path(__file__).parent / 'hooks' / 'post-commit'; OWN_HOOK = 'cairn/tools/post_commit/hooks/post-commit'; _MARK = 'cairn-post-commit-fanout'; _PREDECESSOR = 'cairn-counting-block-door'. `subscribers(repo=None) -> list[Path]` runs `git -C <repo> ls-files -z -- '*/hooks/post-commit'` and returns the repo-relative paths sorted, OWN_HOOK excluded (RuntimeError if git fails). `fire(repo=None, *, timeout_s=600.0) -> list[dict]` runs each subscriber once as `subprocess.run(['bash', str(repo/rel)], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s)` in subscribers() order and returns [{'subscriber': str(rel), 'exit': returncode, 'stderr': last 2000 chars}], echoing each subscriber's stdout; TimeoutExpired records exit 'timeout' and OSError records exit 'unspawnable', and the next subscriber still runs — fire never raises for a subscriber. `hook_path`, `install_hook`, `verify_hook` are COPIED IN SHAPE from cairn/machines/counting_block/hook.py (never imported): hook_path through `rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`; install_hook refuses an existing hook that carries neither _MARK nor _PREDECESSOR (Law 6), says 'already installed, unchanged' for an identical one, else writes HOOK_SOURCE's body and chmods 0o755; verify_hook is green only if the installed hook exists, carries _MARK, is executable and equals HOOK_SOURCE byte for byte.

D3 THE CLI AND THE INSTALLED HOOK. cairn/tools/post_commit/__main__.py: argparse `action` in {fire, install-hook, verify-hook} plus `--repo` (default None = this repo). fire calls fanout.fire(repo), prints `post-commit subscriber <path> exited <exit>: <stderr tail>` to stderr for each non-zero exit, and returns 0 ALWAYS — also when subscribers() itself raises, which is printed and swallowed (the commit has landed; Law 7 loud, never blocking). install-hook / verify-hook print and return exactly as counting_block/__main__.py does. cairn/tools/post_commit/hooks/post-commit is the counting block's hook body with three changes: the first comment line carries `cairn-post-commit-fanout`, the presence guard is `[ -f "$REPO/cairn/tools/post_commit/fanout.py" ] || exit 0`, and the run line is `PYTHONPATH=... "$PY" -m cairn.tools.post_commit fire || true`; it keeps the main-tree-only guard (git-dir == git-common-dir), the bootstrap.sh python, and ends `exit 0`.

D4 THE CHARTER (cairn/tools/post_commit/intention+why.json) takes the shape of cairn/tools/scratch/intention+why.json, key for key: component 'post_commit', runtime_role 'tool', role 'charter', node_class 'tool', public_interface ['cairn.tools.post_commit.fanout'], what, why (git runs one installed post-commit and the counting block held it, so a second listener could only poll HEAD on the beat), entry, invoke (the three CLI actions and the proof command), state_and_history ('A TOOL HOLDS NO STATE OF ITS OWN (Law 6)'), proof, gates, falsifier (this ticket's (1) and (3)), learns and how_it_learns as ONE answer ('It does not; it is a fixed primitive'), traces_to (RULE 1, Law 4, Law 6), owner ('None — a tool has users'), gated_by ['CC']. state.json and history.json beside it come from the crossing door (the BUILDME crossing writes them), never by hand.

D5 THE COUNTING BLOCK HANDS THE INSTALL TO THE FAN-OUT BY IMPORT of its declared public interface (a machine may use a tool; RULE 1 allows exactly cairn.tools.post_commit.fanout). cairn/machines/counting_block/hook.py keeps REPO_ROOT, HOOK_SOURCE and _MARK (they describe its SUBSCRIBER body, which stays at hooks/post-commit, unchanged). Its three functions stay as thin delegations, so callers and test_counting_block.py's tooth (lines 327-351) keep working: hook_path(root) -> fanout.hook_path(root); install_hook(root) -> fanout.install_hook(root); verify_hook(root) -> red with why 'the subscriber body is missing' if HOOK_SOURCE is not a file, else fanout.verify_hook(root). The module docstring says the installed hook is now the fan-out's. counting_block/__main__.py's usage text names the fan-out as the installer; its install-hook/verify-hook actions are unchanged. test_counting_block.py changes its tooth comments only (lines 327 and 335 say the install goes through the fan-out).
decisions.step: modify cairn/machines/counting_block to delegate install-hook and verify-hook

decisions.text: D6 CODEMOTHER'S SUBSCRIBER. cairn/devices/codemother/post_commit.py: `read_commit(repo=None) -> {'hash', 'files', 'message'}` from `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r --root <hash>` (sorted) and `git log -1 --format=%s`. `announce(bus, *, commit, files, message)` calls `bus.post(sender='codemother', to='codemother', channel='personal', verb='commit', why=f'commit {commit[:12]} landed', body={'hash': commit, 'files': list(files), 'message': message})` — the signature at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:361 — then `bus.flush()`. main() does `from cairn.tools.bus_client import reach; announce(reach('codemother'), **read_commit())` (reach at cairn/tools/bus_client/bus_client.py:71 pulses codemother's shim, so post fires _handle_commit -> watch.on_commit in-process). It appends one JSON line {at, hash, outcome} to log_path('codemother') / 'post_commit.jsonl' (cairn.tools.base.address.log_path) and returns 0 if posted, else 1. The precedent for reach+post+flush from a short-lived process is tester/cli.py:293-345 (_announce_seals). cairn/devices/codemother/hooks/post-commit is a bash subscriber with the counting block's guards and bootstrap python; it runs `setsid "$PY" -m cairn.devices.codemother.post_commit </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &` and ends `exit 0`. It detaches because on_commit spreads activations through inference and `git commit` waits on its hook.

D7 THE POLLER GOES (per D1). Delete cairn/devices/codemother/groundloop/ (pulse.py and its __pycache__). In cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_watch.py delete class TestPulse (lines 152-209, the three teeth that patch cairn.devices.codemother.groundloop.pulse), and make the module docstring name watch.py and post_commit.py instead of groundloop/pulse.py. In cairn/devices/codemother/probes/commit_fires_activations.py make the docstring say the commit reaches on_commit through hooks/post-commit -> post_commit.py -> the `commit` verb; its code is unchanged.

D8 THE APPLY, AFTER THE BUILD COMMIT: `python3 -m cairn.tools.post_commit install-hook` replaces the installed counting-block hook (it carries _PREDECESSOR), and `python3 -m cairn.tools.post_commit verify-hook` plus `python3 -m cairn.machines.counting_block verify-hook` must both read green. The next commit is the live fire: counting_block's fold line prints and ~/.cairn/logs/codemother/0/post_commit.jsonl gains a line with that commit's hash.

D31 (settles the D3 gaps): THE HOOK IS GIVEN WHOLE. cairn/tools/post_commit/hooks/post-commit is exactly these bytes (newlines shown as ⏎):⏎#!/usr/bin/env bash⏎# cairn-post-commit-fanout — the one installed post-commit; runs every component's own (e0f318650123).⏎#⏎# Source: cairn/tools/post_commit/hooks/post-commit  (tracked; installed by⏎#         `python3 -m cairn.tools.post_commit install-hook`, verified by `... verify-hook`)⏎#⏎# A component subscribes to the commit by carrying a tracked <component>/hooks/post-commit; the⏎# fan-out finds them with `git ls-files` and runs each once. It never blocks: the commit has⏎# already landed, and a failing subscriber is printed by name and does not stop the next.⏎set -uo pipefail⏎⏎REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || exit 0⏎[ -n "$REPO" ] || exit 0⏎[ "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" = "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" ] || exit 0⏎[ -f "$REPO/cairn/tools/post_commit/fanout.py" ] || exit 0⏎⏎BOOTSTRAP="$REPO/launchers/bootstrap.sh"⏎PY="python3"⏎if [ -r "$BOOTSTRAP" ]; then⏎  # shellcheck source=/dev/null⏎  . "$BOOTSTRAP" && PY="$(cairn_python)"⏎fi⏎⏎cd "$REPO" || exit 0⏎PYTHONPATH="$REPO${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" "$PY" -m cairn.tools.post_commit fire || true⏎exit 0⏎ — written with real newlines, mode 0755. THE CLI OUTPUT IS GIVEN WHOLE. install-hook: print(('installed ' if got['installed'] else 'not installed ') + got['path']); print(f"  {got['why']}"); return 0 if got['installed'] or 'already installed' in got['why'] else 1. verify-hook: print(('green  ' if got['green'] else 'RED    ') + got.get('path', '')); print(f"  {got['why']}"); return 0 if got['green'] else 1. These are the bytes of counting_block/__main__.py's two branches, and fanout's install_hook/verify_hook return the same dict keys {installed|green, path, why} as counting_block/hook.py.

D32 (settles the D4 gap): cairn/tools/post_commit/intention+why.json is a JSON object with exactly these keys, in this order: component ('post_commit'), runtime_role ('tool'), role ('charter'), schema_version (the same string cairn/tools/scratch/intention+why.json carries), node_class ('tool'), node_class_role ('host-seam primitive'), public_interface (['cairn.tools.post_commit.fanout']), what, why, entry, invoke, state_and_history, proof, gates, falsifier, learns, how_it_learns (identical text to learns: 'It does not; it is a fixed primitive.'), traces_to (list: RULE 1, Law 4, Law 6), owner ('None — a tool has users (Law 6)'), gated_by (['CC']), claim_provenance ({role, what, why, public_interface: 'cc-read', traces_to: 'akien'}). All other values are prose strings the builder writes from this ticket's clauses; cairn/tools/scratch/intention+why.json is committed at HEAD as the worked example.

D33 (settles the D6 gaps): main() never unpacks read_commit with **. It calls c = read_commit() and then announce(reach('codemother'), commit=c['hash'], files=c['files'], message=c['message']); read_commit keeps returning {hash, files, message}. The trail line is {at, hash, outcome}: at = UTC ISO-8601 to the second; hash = c['hash'] (absent if read_commit itself raised); outcome is exactly 'posted' when announce returned, otherwise 'failed: <ExceptionType>: <message>' (also printed to stderr). main returns 0 on 'posted', 1 otherwise; the hook detaches it, so the code never reaches the commit.

D34 (settles both unlisted proof steps): the two proofs are NOT written by the build. cairn/tools/post_commit/proofs/test_the_commit_fans_out_to_its_subscribers.py (teeth 1, 1b, 3) and cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_a_commit_reaches_the_watcher.py (teeth 2, 2b, 2c, 4) were committed red at a5ce4acc before this rehearsal, and their bytes are the spec the build answers. The builder runs each, edits neither, and the build is done when both exit 0 and are sealed (bin/cairn test --seal <proof>).
